title: Capacity arbitrage routing: playbook & mini-proforma (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook + mini-proforma for extracting 'capacity arbitrage' savings from smart routing decisions. The goal: concrete routing heuristics and a small spreadsheet proforma teams can copy and adapt to estimate marginal $/token savings when mixing spot, on-demand, reserved (dedicated) and cross-region fallbacks.

Audience:
- Product Optimize team (primary)
- Serving/runtime and SRE (for feasibility + telemetry hooks)
- Solutions engineering (customer proformas)

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Treat routing as an arbitrage problem: match request SLO and quality constraints to the cheapest available capacity bucket (spot, on-demand, reserved) while preserving SLA via fallbacks.
- Use a discrete-tiering approach (fastest-optimized local reserved -> local spot -> remote reserved -> remote spot -> degrade-to-lower-model) instead of trying to compute continuous expected-cost for every request.
- Maintain a simple spreadsheet with per-tier unit-cost, expected latency delta, failure/eviction probability, and fallback-stack cost to compute expected cost and risk-adjusted savings.

Key definitions and assumptions used in the model:
1) Unit cost definitions (example baseline numbers; teams should replace with live pricing):
   - local_reserved_unit = $0.008 per 1k tokens (stable throughput, SLO help)
   - local_spot_unit = $0.0035 per 1k tokens (cheaper but eviction risk)
   - remote_reserved_unit = $0.007 per 1k tokens + egress delta
   - remote_spot_unit = $0.0030 per 1k tokens + egress delta
   - lower_quality_model_unit = $0.002 per 1k tokens (fallback model with worse quality)
   - egress_penalty_ms = 18 ms typical; add regional latency cost when estimating SLO hit probability

2) Failure modes:
   - spot_eviction_rate (per minute) — empirical, pulled from capacity telemetry; default assumption here = 0.6% per minute under heavy cluster churn
   - remote_network_flakiness = 0.2% request failure

3) Latency SLO bucketing for routing decision:
   - strict: end-to-end p95 < 250ms -> prefer local reserved, only use local spot if successful warm-kv and prefix-cached
   - medium: p95 < 600ms -> local spot or remote reserved acceptable
   - elastic: p95 < 1.5s -> can route to remote spot or lower-quality model

Mini-proforma algorithm (stepwise):
1) For each request class (e.g., chat-llama-13b-short, embeddings-batch-512): define token distribution (avg prompt + gen tokens) and latency SLO bucket.
2) For each candidate tier, compute:
   - raw_unit_cost = base_unit (from pricing table)
   - expected_fallback_cost = sum_over_possible_failures(prob_failure * fallback_chain_expected_cost)
   - expected_total_cost = raw_unit_cost + expected_fallback_cost
   - latency_risk = probability that chosen tier will exceed SLO (function of baseline latency + eviction-induced retries + network)
3) Pick the tier with lowest expected_total_cost among tiers that keep latency_risk below an acceptable threshold (team-defined; default 0.5%)

Quick example (text CSV snippet you can paste into a sheet):
tier,base_unit_usd_per_1k_tokens,eviction_prob_per_min,avg_egress_ms,fallback_chain_cost_usd_per_1k,expected_total_cost_usd_per_1k,notes
local_reserved,0.008,0.0001,6,0.0000,0.008,stable
local_spot,0.0035,0.006,6,0.0015,0.0050,eviction => retry remote_reserved
remote_reserved,0.007,0.0002,24,0.0003,0.0073,egress cost included
remote_spot,0.0030,0.005,24,0.0017,0.0047,cheapest but riskier
lower_model,0.002,0.0000,5,0.0000,0.002,quality degrade

Sensitivity knobs to explore in the sheet (columns to include):
- SLO_threshold_ms (toggles which tiers are eligible)
- eviction_rate_adjustment (for peak hours)
- price_delta_spot/reserved (simulate bulk discounts or marketplace changes)
- multi-region_egress_cost (unit $/token or fixed per-call)

Heuristic routing rules (early version for runtime and routing team):
- If request_class.SLO == strict: prefer local_reserved; allow local_spot only when prefix-cache hit and observed spot_eviction_rate < 1% over past 10m.
- For medium: use cost-ranked tiers but disallow remote_spot if estimated SLO miss rate > 0.75% or if client is in APAC and remote is NA (latency delta > 60ms).
- For elastic: maximize expected savings but cap fallback depth to 2 (i.e., local_spot -> remote_reserved -> stop).
- Implement rapid backoff: if recent spot eviction rate crosses threshold, temporarily route new sessions off spot for X minutes and surface an alert.

Telemetry & instrumentation required (runtime/SRE asks):
- Per-tier request counts, token counts, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and failure rates (evictions, network).
- Per-request routing decision metadata: chosen_tier, fallback_chain_taken, total_cost_estimate_at-decision-time, actual_cost_realized.
- Short-window (1m/5m/15m) and longer-window (1h/24h) eviction stats per region+instance type.
- Small priming probe: proactively send small probe traffic to spot machines when idle to warm kernel caches for chosen models (measure improvement).

Open questions / TODOs (prioritized):
- [P0] How to model multi-token generation variance? Current proforma uses average tokens; need distribution-aware expected cost (Monte Carlo sampling). Owner: Jamal.
- [P1] Should we charge customer-facing APIs with blended expected cost or realized cost? (billing implications). Ping finance.
- [P2] Can runtime expose real-time spot_eviction_score for a candidate instance so router makes per-request decision? Work with serving-runtime.
- [P3] Egress-cost model: should we attribute egress ms to token cost directly or treat as independent SLA penalty?

Proposed next steps (concrete):
1) Product Optimize: finalize baseline pricing table (1 week) -> I (Priya) take ownership.
2) Runtime: expose per-instance eviction_rate and simple health probe endpoint (2 sprints).
3) SRE: add per-tier telemetry streams to observability pipeline; sliceable by region and model (1 sprint).
4) Build a shared spreadsheet template (copyable CSV above) + a tiny notebook that runs Monte Carlo sensitivity (2 weeks).

Notes to solutions engineering (how to use this with customer):
- Start with the customer’s 7-day token profile and SLO. Run the proforma to show expected savings (baseline vs routing). Clearly show downside risk (probability of SLO miss and expected degrade).
- For high-regulated customers, prefer deterministic reserved capacity (show tradeoff).

Attachment ideas for the sheet (columns):
- request_class, avg_prompt_tokens, avg_gen_tokens, p95_slo_ms, eligible_tiers, chosen_tier, raw_unit_cost, fallback_prob, fallback_expected_cost, expected_total_cost, expected_latency_ms, realized_cost_last_24h

Quick change log (so reviewers know doc history):
- 2025-02-18 initial skeleton (Priya)
- 2025-02-25 added CSV snippet and heuristics (Jamal)
- 2025-03-04 sensitivity knobs and TODOs updated (Sofia)

If you test this, please paste results to the Confluence page linked above and tag the doc owners. This is intentionally light on math — we will add Monte Carlo and distribution work after initial telemetry is live.

Unresolved design decisions to debate in the next sync:
- Max fallback depth tradeoffs (cost vs SLA exposure)
- Whether to normalize token unit to per-1000 or per-100 for markets with short prompt lengths
- How to integrate cost-optimized routing signals with rollout/AB test framework in Console

End of draft.

-- Priya
